identifying_description: Short evening dress of black silk with heavy embroidery: thin straps; full dress embroidered in patterned stripes with pink, blue, brown, orange, and white sequins, wood beads, and metal beads; mid stomach portion has no lining.
web_text: Algerian-born, French-based Yves Saint Laurent drew inspiration from a wide variety of cultural sources throughout his career, and correlated such cultural borrowing to his individual belief in modernity as synonymous with cultural diversity. But, as instances of cultural appropriation are reconsidered in light of the demise of colonial empires and the imbalances of power forged by colonization, imperialism, and enslavement, the designer’s practice of cultural borrowing may be reexamined as well. Saint Laurent often drew inspiration from his childhood experiences in Algeria, where he was a member of the French colonial classes. The clothing of the Bambara in Mali – a French colony until the 1960s -- inspired these beadwork mini dresses, which are thus a reflection of French colonization as well as Saint Laurent’s design practice.
